arm_set.name: v4_final_five_arm
arm_set.dropped_arms_reason: the ch25 gate criteria name a fixed inspection route, random views and a systematic coverage sweep, and those three are all flown. The other baselines are SELECTION evidence from the validation split (ACTIVE-MCBR-E005) and were never gate comparators; flying all eleven would be 330 flights and would inform no criterion.
arm_set.reason: four gate arms plus one attribution control. Run 1 flew the same four gate arms on 20 worlds; run 3 flies them on 30 fresh worlds and adds the V3-protocol control.
decides_criteria: beats fixed views on actual hidden-state reconstruction

declared_limitation: The three baseline arms fly the INCUMBENT execution protocol, exactly as they did in runs 1 and 2, because the protocol is part of the production mechanism under test and not part of the shared budget. A coverage-sweep arm carrying the V4 protocol is therefore NOT flown, and this run cannot separate "MCBR's ranking beats a coverage sweep" from "the production stack beats a coverage sweep". The gate criterion is the second statement, and that is what a PASS here would mean. This limitation is declared before the run and is reported with the verdict whatever the verdict is.
power_note: Sized before the run from the MEASURED validation effect, not from a wish. On the 40 validation worlds the frozen mechanism beat coverage-only by +0.2406 with a 95 % paired CI of [+0.1072, +0.3757], a half width of about 0.13 at n = 40, and beat the V3 protocol by +0.3034 [+0.1808, +0.4279]. The per-world outcome on this family is exactly binary (about 0.78 when the defect is read, 0.000 when it is not), so the primary metric is a success rate and the paired CI half width scales as 1/sqrt(n): about 0.15 at n = 30. An effect of +0.24 is therefore separable at n = 30, while the +0.0094 tie run 2 measured was not separable at n = 60. Cost enters the choice honestly and only after the power argument: at the 90.1 s per flight measured on this host in a dry run on a development world, 5 arms x 30 worlds is 150 flights, about 3.8 h, against about 7.5 h for 60 worlds. Thirty worlds is enough for this effect; sixty would buy resolution this comparison does not need.
decision_rule: Unit = one world, paired across arms. PRODUCTION beats a comparator on a metric iff the lower bound of the 95 % paired percentile-bootstrap CI over worlds (4000 resamples, rng seed 20260919) of the benefit (PRODUCTION better = positive) is above 0. Identical rule, resample count and seed to runs 1 and 2. Gate I4 passes iff every criterion passes: the closed loop, beats fixed views, beats random views, beats coverage-only on hidden_state_error_improvement, and beats fixed, random AND coverage on info_per_time AND info_per_kj. A TIE WITH COVERAGE IS A FAIL. No numeric margin is invented, and every paired CI is reported whatever its sign, including the V3-protocol control, which decides nothing.
